pinyin: xiǎo mǐ jiā bù qiāng
literal: millet · plus · rifle
natural: millet and rifles

meaning.en: A shorthand for the Communist forces' poor equipment in the 1930s-40s: they fought on a diet of millet with basic infantry rifles, yet prevailed.
meaning.zh: 形容中共军队早年装备简陋、给养艰苦：靠小米充饥、步枪作战，最终取得胜利。

equivalents: a shoestring army
fighting on millet and rifles

examples.zh: 爷爷常说，当年的八路军就是靠小米加步枪打败了装备精良的对手。
examples.en: Grandpa often says the Eighth Route Army beat a far better-armed enemy on millet and rifles.

examples.zh: 展览馆里陈列着小米加步枪时期的旧物件。
examples.en: The museum displays objects from the millet-and-rifles years.

examples.zh: 创业初期，我们是小米加步枪，靠的就是一股拼劲。
examples.en: In the early start-up days we ran on millet and rifles: all we had was drive.

usage.en: Used historically for the Yan'an and War of Resistance era, and figuratively today for a poorly resourced team that competes with a better-equipped rival. It is often paired with 飞机加大炮 ('aircraft and artillery') for the other side. Neutral. No single originator is given, because it was common wartime and later political parlance.
usage.zh: 多指延安与抗战、解放战争时期，今天也比喻资源有限却能与装备精良者竞争的团队。常与“飞机加大炮”对举。中性。该说法是当时和后来的通用政治用语，故不标明单一出处。

text: 一张白纸，好画最新最美的图画
pinyin: yī zhāng bái zhǐ, hǎo huà zuì xīn zuì měi de tú huà
literal: one · sheet · blank · paper, easy to · paint · most · new · most · beautiful · 's · picture
natural: on a blank sheet of paper, the newest and most beautiful picture can be painted

meaning.en: A blank sheet is the best surface for the freshest and finest picture: a people with little to start with can build something entirely new.
meaning.zh: 一张白纸没有负担，最容易画出最新最美的图画；比喻起点低、基础薄，反而便于创造全新的事业。

equivalents: a blank slate to build on
a clean sheet for a fresh start

examples.zh: 新校区的规划者说，一张白纸，好画最新最美的图画。
examples.en: The planners of the new campus said a blank sheet is the best place to paint the newest and most beautiful picture.

examples.zh: 他把初创公司看作一张白纸，好画最新最美的图画。
examples.en: He sees the start-up as a blank sheet on which the newest, finest picture can be painted.

origin.source: 毛泽东《介绍一个合作社》（1958年）

story.en: In a 1958 article introducing a cooperative, Mao Zedong wrote that the Chinese people were 'poor and blank', like a blank sheet of paper with no burden, on which the newest and most beautiful pictures could be drawn.
story.zh: 毛泽东在1958年《介绍一个合作社》一文中说，中国人民“一穷二白”，好像一张白纸，没有负担，好写最新最美的文字，好画最新最美的画图。

usage.en: Quoted as an optimistic view of starting from scratch, in news, speeches and essays. Often cut to 一张白纸. Positive, formal. Written in 1958; Mao used it of the Chinese people being 'poor and blank', which in his view made them receptive to new ideas.
usage.zh: 常用来表达白手起家、从头开始的乐观态度，见于新闻、讲话和作文。常简作“一张白纸”。褒义，正式。1958年毛泽东用以说明中国人民“一穷二白”，正因如此易于接受新思想。

text: 四海翻腾云水怒，五洲震荡风雷激
pinyin: sì hǎi fān téng yún shuǐ nù, wǔ zhōu zhèn dàng fēng léi jī
literal: four · seas · churn · clouds · waters · rage, five · continents · shake · wind · thunder · fierce
natural: the four seas churn, clouds and waters rage; the five continents shake, wind and thunder surge

meaning.en: A couplet picturing a world in violent upheaval, with seas, clouds, winds and thunder all in turmoil.
meaning.zh: 形容世界风云激荡、局势剧烈动荡，如同海翻云怒、风雷滚滚。

equivalents: the whole world in turmoil
a world shaken to its foundations

examples.zh: 评论员引用“四海翻腾云水怒，五洲震荡风雷激”来形容那个动荡的年代。
examples.en: The commentator quoted 'the four seas churn, clouds and waters rage' to describe that turbulent era.

examples.zh: 国际局势复杂多变，真有四海翻腾云水怒，五洲震荡风雷激之感。
examples.en: The international situation is so fluid it truly feels like the four seas churning and the five continents shaking.

origin.source: 毛泽东《满江红·和郭沫若同志》（1963年）

story.en: Mao Zedong wrote this poem in January 1963 in reply to Guo Moruo; the couplet reads '四海翻腾云水怒，五洲震荡风雷激'.
story.zh: 毛泽东1963年1月作《满江红·和郭沫若同志》，上阕有“四海翻腾云水怒，五洲震荡风雷激”。

usage.en: Quoted in commentary on global upheaval, either as the full couplet or in halves. Literary and formal; it is a poem line, not a slogan. In the poem it refers to the revolutionary and anti-colonial movements of the early 1960s.
usage.zh: 评论国际风云变幻时引用，可引全联，也可只引一句。文学性强，正式；是诗句而非口号。词中所指是20世纪60年代初的世界革命和反殖民浪潮。

pinyin: dào zhōng liú jī shuǐ, làng è fēi zhōu
literal: reach · mid · stream · strike · water, waves · hold back · flying · boat
natural: strike the water in midstream until the waves stop a speeding boat

meaning.en: To swim out into the middle of the current and fight the waves with such force that they check a speeding boat; a picture of youthful daring and courage against great odds.
meaning.zh: 到江心奋力游泳，激起的浪头能阻住飞快的船；比喻青年人敢于搏击风浪、勇往直前。

equivalents: to take on the current head-on
to brave the waves

examples.zh: 毕业典礼上，校长引用“到中流击水，浪遏飞舟”勉励同学勇闯新天地。
examples.en: At graduation the principal quoted 'strike the water in midstream, let the waves hold back the boat' to urge students to venture boldly.

examples.zh: 他读到“到中流击水，浪遏飞舟”，想起了少年时在湘江游泳的情景。
examples.en: Reading 'to strike the water in midstream, waves checking the speeding boats', he recalled swimming in the Xiang River as a boy.

story.en: Mao Zedong wrote this poem in 1925 as he left Changsha; it ends '曾记否，到中流击水，浪遏飞舟'.
story.zh: 毛泽东1925年离开长沙时作《沁园春·长沙》，结尾为“曾记否，到中流击水，浪遏飞舟”。

usage.en: Quoted to encourage young people or to praise daring. The short form 浪遏飞舟 is also an entry, but this is the full line with its first half. In the poem it follows 曾记否; the whole line sums up the poet's youthful confidence. Positive, literary.
usage.zh: 多用于勉励青年或赞扬敢闯敢拼。四字的“浪遏飞舟”另有词条，这里是带上半句的完整诗句。原词中紧接“曾记否”，抒发词人青年时期的豪情。褒义，文学性强。

text: 人民群众是真正的英雄
pinyin: rén mín qún zhòng shì zhēn zhèng de yīng xióng
literal: people · masses · are · truly · 's · heroes
natural: the people are the real heroes

meaning.en: A political saying that history is made by ordinary people, not by a few great leaders.
meaning.zh: 政治话语：历史是由普通群众创造的，而不是少数杰出人物。

equivalents: the people are the real heroes
history is made by ordinary people

examples.zh: 抗洪胜利后，报道强调人民群众是真正的英雄。
examples.en: After the flood was beaten, reports stressed that the ordinary people were the real heroes.

examples.zh: 领导在讲话中说：人民群众是真正的英雄。
examples.en: In his speech the leader said that the people are the real heroes.

usage.en: Common in political speeches and news. It paraphrases Mao Zedong's idea of the masses as the makers of history (his 1941 preface to 'Rural Surveys' calls them 'the real heroes'); the exact wording here is the later set form, so no origin is given. Formal.
usage.zh: 常见于政治讲话和新闻报道。它概括毛泽东关于群众创造历史的观点（1941年《〈农村调查〉的序言和跋》称群众“是真正的英雄”），但此处是后来固定下来的说法，故不标出处。正式。

pinyin: tiān xià dà luàn, xíng shì dà hǎo
literal: under heaven · greatly · chaotic, situation · greatly · good
natural: great disorder under heaven, the situation is excellent

meaning.en: A Cultural Revolution-era slogan claiming that widespread upheaval is a good sign because it clears the way for a new order.
meaning.zh: 文化大革命时期的口号，认为社会大动荡是好事，可以破旧立新、达到新的秩序。

equivalents: chaos is a good sign
turmoil as opportunity

examples.zh: 历史书介绍了“天下大乱，形势大好”这类当时流行的口号。
examples.en: The history book introduces slogans of the time such as 'great disorder under heaven, the situation is excellent'.

examples.zh: 他讽刺说，不能把天下大乱，形势大好当作办事原则。
examples.en: He remarked wryly that 'great disorder, excellent situation' should not be a working principle.

usage.en: Today a historical reference to the Cultural Revolution (1966-76), or an ironic remark when someone claims a chaotic situation is actually good. The idea echoes Mao's remarks about 'great disorder leading to great order' (天下大乱，达到天下大治); the exact slogan has no single source given here. The first half 天下大乱 is also a separate entry.
usage.zh: 今天多作对文化大革命（1966—1976）的历史引用，或讽刺把乱局说成好事的人。其思路与毛泽东“天下大乱，达到天下大治”的说法相关，此处不标明单一出处。上半句“天下大乱”另有词条。

text: 宁要社会主义的草，不要资本主义的苗
pinyin: nìng yào shè huì zhǔ yì de cǎo, bù yào zī běn zhǔ yì de miáo
literal: rather · want · socialism · 's · weeds, not · want · capitalism · 's · seedlings
natural: better socialist weeds than capitalist seedlings

meaning.en: A slogan of the Cultural Revolution period meaning that political correctness mattered more than economic results.
meaning.zh: 文化大革命时期的口号，意思是政治路线比经济效益更重要，宁可贫穷落后也不走资本主义道路。

equivalents: ideology over results
better weeds of the right kind than crops of the wrong kind

examples.zh: 这本书分析了“宁要社会主义的草，不要资本主义的苗”这类口号对经济的影响。
examples.en: The book analyses how slogans like 'better socialist weeds than capitalist seedlings' affected the economy.

examples.zh: 他用“宁要社会主义的草，不要资本主义的苗”来说明当时的极端思潮。
examples.en: He used 'better socialist weeds than capitalist seedlings' to illustrate the extreme thinking of the time.

usage.en: A historical reference to the 1960s-70s, now often quoted to illustrate how ideology was once placed above productivity. No single originator is given. Neutral, formal.
usage.zh: 多作为对20世纪六七十年代的历史引用，今天常用来说明当年把意识形态置于生产力之上。不标明单一出处。中性，正式。

pinyin: gē zī běn zhǔ yì wěi ba
literal: cut · capitalism · tail
natural: cut off the capitalist tail

meaning.en: A political campaign term for curbing private plots, sideline production and small trade, which were labelled remnants of capitalism.
meaning.zh: 政治运动用语，指限制自留地、家庭副业和小商贩，把它们当作资本主义残余加以割除。

equivalents: to clamp down on private enterprise
to prune away private sidelines

examples.zh: 那几年农民养几只鸡，也可能被说成要割资本主义尾巴。
examples.en: In those years even keeping a few chickens could be called a capitalist tail that had to be cut.

examples.zh: 纪录片讲述了割资本主义尾巴运动对农村生活的影响。
examples.en: The documentary describes how the campaign to cut the capitalist tail affected village life.

usage.en: A historical term, used mostly for the 1960s-70s, when private plots and sidelines were restricted. It appears today in history and economics discussions. The 尾巴 is the 'tail' of private economic activity. Neutral, formal. No individual originator is given.
usage.zh: 历史用语，主要指20世纪六七十年代限制自留地和家庭副业的做法，今天见于历史和经济讨论。“尾巴”指私人经济活动的残余。中性，正式。不标明单一出处。

pinyin: hěn dòu sī zì yī shǎn niàn
literal: fiercely · struggle · self-interest · word · one · flash · thought
natural: fight fiercely against the 'self' in every fleeting thought

meaning.en: A Cultural Revolution slogan urging people to root out even the briefest selfish thought and put the collective first.
meaning.zh: 文化大革命时期的口号，要求人们对头脑中一闪而过的私心杂念也要坚决克服，凡事先公后私。

equivalents: root out every selfish thought
self-criticism of even a fleeting thought

examples.zh: 历史课上，老师解释了“狠斗私字一闪念”这个口号的背景。
examples.en: In history class the teacher explained the background of the slogan 'fight the self in every fleeting thought'.

examples.zh: 他说，狠斗私字一闪念的年代，人人都要自我检讨。
examples.en: He said that in the years of 'fight the self in every fleeting thought', everyone had to make self-criticisms.

usage.en: A historical reference to the late 1960s, usually in discussions of the period's political culture or in irony about excessive self-criticism. 私 is 'self-interest'. Neutral, formal.
usage.zh: 历史引用，多指20世纪60年代后期，常见于谈论当时政治文化的场合，或讽刺过度的自我批判。“私”指私心。中性，正式。

text: 千万不要忘记阶级斗争
pinyin: qiān wàn bù yào wàng jì jí jí dòu zhēng
literal: absolutely · must not · forget · class · struggle
natural: never forget class struggle

meaning.en: A political slogan warning that class struggle continues under socialism and must always be kept in mind.
meaning.zh: 政治口号，提醒人们社会主义社会中阶级斗争仍然存在，必须时刻牢记。

equivalents: never forget class struggle
always bear class struggle in mind

examples.zh: 学校墙上曾刷着“千万不要忘记阶级斗争”的大字标语。
examples.en: The school wall once bore the big-character slogan 'never forget class struggle'.

examples.zh: 这篇回忆录写道，千万不要忘记阶级斗争成了当时的口头禅。
examples.en: The memoir recalls that 'never forget class struggle' became a catchphrase of the time.

origin.source: 毛泽东在中共八届十中全会上的讲话（1962年9月）

story.en: Mao Zedong told the Tenth Plenum of the Eighth Central Committee in September 1962 that class struggle must be talked about 'every year, every month, every day', and the plenum's communiqué carried the call.
story.zh: 1962年9月，毛泽东在中共八届十中全会上强调阶级斗争要“年年讲、月月讲、天天讲”，全会公报也写入了这一提法。

usage.en: Historical reference to the 1960s-70s. Mao Zedong raised it at the Tenth Plenum of the Eighth Central Committee in September 1962. The related entry 以阶级斗争为纲 ('take class struggle as the key link') covers the policy line. Neutral, formal.
usage.zh: 对20世纪六七十年代的历史引用。毛泽东在1962年9月中共八届十中全会上提出。相关词条“以阶级斗争为纲”则是路线性提法。中性，正式。

pinyin: yī jù dǐng yī wàn jù
literal: one · sentence · equals · ten thousand · sentences
natural: one sentence is worth ten thousand

meaning.en: A Cultural Revolution-era formula for the supreme authority of the leader's words: a single sentence outweighs ten thousand of anyone else's.
meaning.zh: 文化大革命时期对领袖言论权威的说法：他的一句话抵得上别人的一万句。

equivalents: his word is worth ten thousand of ours
one word carries the weight of ten thousand

examples.zh: 那个年代，“一句顶一万句”成了人人挂在嘴边的话。
examples.en: In those years 'one sentence is worth ten thousand' was on everyone's lips.

examples.zh: 刘震云的小说《一句顶一万句》写的却是普通人想找个说得上话的人。
examples.en: Liu Zhenyun's novel 'One Sentence Is Worth Ten Thousand' is about ordinary people seeking someone to talk to.

usage.en: A historical phrase from the late 1960s, associated with Lin Biao's remarks on Mao's words in 1966 (the exact wording varies by source, so no origin is given). Today it is also known as the title of Liu Zhenyun's 2009 novel, where it is used in a very different sense. Neutral, formal.
usage.zh: 20世纪60年代后期的历史用语，与1966年林彪评价毛泽东言论的说法有关（各处措辞略有出入，故不标出处）。今天它也是刘震云2009年同名小说的书名，含义已大不相同。中性，正式。

pinyin: yuè qióng yuè guāng róng
literal: the more · poor · the more · glorious
natural: the poorer, the more glorious

meaning.en: A Cultural Revolution-era slogan that treated poverty as a mark of political virtue, since the poor were seen as the most revolutionary.
meaning.zh: 文化大革命时期的口号，把贫穷当作政治上的光荣，认为越穷越革命。

equivalents: poverty as a badge of honour
the poorer the prouder

examples.zh: 奶奶回忆说，那时候流行“越穷越光荣”，谁富裕谁反而心虚。
examples.en: Grandma recalls that 'the poorer the more glorious' was popular then, and anyone well-off felt uneasy.

examples.zh: 今天没有人再会说越穷越光荣了。
examples.en: Nobody says 'the poorer the more glorious' any more.

usage.en: Historical reference to the 1960s-70s, mostly quoted with irony today, often set against Deng Xiaoping-era 'to get rich is glorious' (致富光荣). The exact origin of the wording is unclear, so none is given. Casual to neutral.
usage.zh: 对20世纪六七十年代的历史引用，今天多带讽刺意味，常与改革开放时期的“致富光荣”相对照。其确切出处不明，故不标出处。口语到中性。

pinyin: zǎo qǐng shì wǎn huì bào
literal: morning · ask for instructions · evening · report
natural: ask for instructions in the morning, report back in the evening

meaning.en: A Cultural Revolution-era ritual in which people paid homage to Mao's portrait each morning and reported on their thinking each evening.
meaning.zh: 文化大革命时期的一种做法：每天早上向毛泽东像请示，晚上汇报思想和工作。

equivalents: morning pledge and evening report
ritual daily loyalty reporting

examples.zh: 回忆文章里写到，当年的“早请示晚汇报”要在毛主席像前进行。
examples.en: The memoir describes how 'morning instructions, evening reports' were done before a portrait of Mao.

examples.zh: 他笑称现在的领导要求汇报太多，简直是早请示晚汇报。
examples.en: He joked that the boss demands so many reports that it is like morning instructions and evening reports.

usage.en: A historical term for the practice of 1966-76. Today it is also used jokingly of any excessive reporting to a superior. Neutral, formal.
usage.zh: 对1966—1976年间做法的历史用语。今天也可以开玩笑地形容向上级汇报得太频繁。中性，正式。

pinyin: dà gàn kuài shàng
literal: all-out · work · fast · go up
natural: work all out and launch quickly

meaning.en: A mass-campaign term for tackling a project with great energy and haste, often with little planning.
meaning.zh: 群众运动用语，指干劲十足、迅速上马地搞一项工程或事业，往往缺乏周密计划。

equivalents: go all out and build fast
to push ahead at full tilt

examples.zh: 那个年代工地上到处是大干快上的标语。
examples.en: In those years building sites were hung with 'work all out and launch fast' slogans.

examples.zh: 项目不能只靠大干快上，还要有科学论证。
examples.en: Projects cannot rely on all-out haste alone; they need sound feasibility studies.

usage.en: The spirit of the 1958 Great Leap Forward and later campaigns. Today it can be neutral praise for energy, but is often used critically about rushed, unplanned projects. No single originator is given. Neutral, formal.
usage.zh: 1958年大跃进及后来各类运动的精神。今天可以是对干劲的中性称赞，更常用来批评仓促上马、缺乏计划的做法。不标明单一出处。中性，正式。

pinyin: gēn zhèng miáo hóng
literal: root · straight · sprout · red
natural: straight roots and a red sprout

meaning.en: Describes someone of impeccable class background and political credentials, as the PRC once judged them: a worker, poor-peasant or revolutionary family.
meaning.zh: 形容出身（家庭成分）好、政治上可靠，旧时指出身于工人、贫农或革命家庭。

equivalents: of impeccable pedigree
from a good family background

examples.zh: 那个年代，根正苗红的人才能参军、入党。
examples.en: Back then only those who were 'straight of root and red of sprout' could join the army or the Party.

examples.zh: 他自嘲不是根正苗红，当年连入团都很困难。
examples.en: He joked that he was not 'red of sprout' and found it hard even to join the Youth League.

usage.en: Pre-1980s class-background language. Now it is mostly used of an official or successor with an impeccable background, sometimes playfully or sarcastically. 根 refers to family background and 苗 to the individual. Neutral to casual.
usage.zh: 改革开放前的成分论用语。今天多用于出身背景无可挑剔的干部或接班人，有时带戏谑或讽刺。“根”指家庭出身，“苗”指本人。中性到口语。

pinyin: gé mìng de luó sī dīng
literal: revolution · 's · screw
natural: a screw of the revolution

meaning.en: A model worker's image of oneself as a small but essential part of a great machine, ready to serve wherever needed.
meaning.zh: 把自己比作大机器上小而重要的螺丝钉，愿意在任何岗位上尽责。

equivalents: a cog in the machine
a small but vital part

examples.zh: 他以做一颗革命的螺丝钉为荣，默默在岗位上工作了四十年。
examples.en: He was proud to be a screw of the revolution and worked quietly at his post for forty years.

examples.zh: 学雷锋活动中，同学们都说要做革命的螺丝钉。
examples.en: During the Learn from Lei Feng campaign the students all said they wanted to be screws of the revolution.

usage.en: Associated with the soldier Lei Feng (1940-62), whose published diary compares a person to a screw in a machine; the wording was spread by the 1960s Learn from Lei Feng campaign, and the diary's exact text is open to dispute, so no origin is given. Now often used for dedicated ordinary workers. Positive, formal.
usage.zh: 与战士雷锋（1940—1962）相关，其出版的日记把人比作机器上的螺丝钉，经1960年代学雷锋运动传开。日记原文有争议，故不标出处。今天常用来称赞默默奉献的普通劳动者。褒义，正式。

pinyin: gé mìng zì yǒu hòu lái rén
literal: revolution · naturally · has · later · comers · people
natural: the revolution will have successors

meaning.en: A line expressing confidence that the cause will be carried on by the next generation.
meaning.zh: 表示对事业后继有人的信心，下一代一定会接过前人的事业。

equivalents: the torch will be passed on
there will always be successors

examples.zh: 老教授退休时说，革命自有后来人，他对年轻一代充满信心。
examples.en: On retiring the old professor said the cause will have successors and he trusted the younger generation.

examples.zh: 看着学生们接手实验室，他欣慰地想：革命自有后来人。
examples.en: Watching his students take over the lab, he thought contentedly: the cause will have successors.

story.en: The line is sung by the railway worker Li Yuhe in the modern Peking opera 'The Red Lantern', which became one of the eight model operas.
story.zh: 该句是现代京剧《红灯记》中铁路工人李玉和的唱词，此剧后来成为“样板戏”之一。

date.zh: 中华人民共和国 · 约1964年

usage.en: Quoted when handing a cause or craft on to young people, now often free of its original political meaning. The line is sung by Li Yuhe in the model opera 'The Red Lantern' (《红灯记》); the opera was revised and famous in the mid-1960s, and several people shared in its creation. Positive, formal.
usage.zh: 在把事业或手艺交给年轻人时引用，如今常脱离原来的政治含义。该句出自现代京剧《红灯记》中李玉和的唱词，该剧于1960年代中期修改定型而闻名，创作者不止一人。褒义，正式。

text: 农业学大寨，工业学大庆
pinyin: nóng yè xué dà zhài, gōng yè xué dà qìng
literal: agriculture · learn from · Dazhai, industry · learn from · Daqing
natural: in agriculture learn from Dazhai, in industry learn from Daqing

meaning.en: A 1960s-70s national slogan pairing two model communities: the Dazhai brigade for farming and the Daqing oilfield for industry.
meaning.zh: 20世纪六七十年代的全国性口号，把大寨（农业）和大庆（工业）树为学习榜样。

equivalents: learn from Dazhai and Daqing
follow the model farm and the model oilfield

examples.zh: 展览回顾了“农业学大寨，工业学大庆”的群众运动。
examples.en: The exhibition looks back at the mass campaign 'in agriculture learn from Dazhai, in industry learn from Daqing'.

examples.zh: 老厂长至今记得当年“农业学大寨，工业学大庆”的口号。
examples.en: The old factory director still remembers the slogan 'in agriculture learn from Dazhai, in industry learn from Daqing'.

usage.en: Historical reference. Dazhai is a Shanxi village and Daqing an oilfield in Heilongjiang, both promoted from 1964 onwards; Dazhai's model was later widely criticised, while Daqing's spirit is still celebrated. Neutral, formal. No single wording origin is given.
usage.zh: 历史引用。大寨是山西的一个村庄，大庆是黑龙江的油田，二者自1964年起被树为典型；后来大寨经验受到广泛批评，大庆精神则至今受到推崇。中性，正式。不标明单一出处。

text: 天大地大不如党的恩情大
pinyin: tiān dà dì dà bù rú dǎng de ēn qíng dà
literal: heaven · big · earth · big · not as good as · Party · 's · kindness · big
natural: heaven is great and earth is great, but not as great as the Party's kindness

meaning.en: A song-slogan expressing gratitude to the Party, claiming its kindness outweighs heaven and earth.
meaning.zh: 表达对党感恩之情的歌词式口号，说党的恩情比天地还大。

equivalents: a debt of gratitude greater than heaven and earth

examples.zh: 老人唱起了“天大地大不如党的恩情大”，眼里含着泪光。
examples.en: The old man sang 'heaven and earth are great but not as great as the Party's kindness', tears in his eyes.

examples.zh: 展览中播放着“天大地大不如党的恩情大”的老歌。
examples.en: The exhibition plays the old song 'heaven and earth are great but not as great as the Party's kindness'.

usage.en: Known from songs and slogans of the 1950s-60s, in the same pattern as the folk 天大地大不如爹娘恩情大 ('not as great as parents' kindness'). Used today in historical and nostalgic settings. Positive, formal. No single author is given.
usage.zh: 常见于20世纪五六十年代的歌曲和标语，句式仿民间说法“天大地大不如爹娘恩情大”。今天多用于历史回顾和怀旧场合。褒义，正式。不标明单一作者。

pinyin: shéi shuō nǚ zǐ bù rú nán
literal: who · says · women · not as good as · men
natural: who says women are not as good as men

meaning.en: A rhetorical question that rejects the old belief that women are inferior to men.
meaning.zh: 反问句，驳斥旧时女子不如男子的看法。

equivalents: who says women can't do it
women hold up half the sky

examples.zh: 她拿下了全国冠军，谁说女子不如男！
examples.en: She won the national title, so who says women are not as good as men!

examples.zh: 女工程师在团队里担起大梁，真是谁说女子不如男。
examples.en: The woman engineer carried the team: who says women are not as good as men.

usage.en: A casual line of encouragement or pride, much used when a woman succeeds in a field once seen as male. It spread widely through the Henan-opera song of Hua Mulan from the 1950s and the 1956 film, though the exact wording of the original line is not certain here, so no origin is given. Positive.
usage.zh: 口语中用来鼓励女性或表达自豪，常见于女性在传统男性领域取得成就时。20世纪50年代豫剧《花木兰》唱段及1956年电影使之广为流传，但原句具体出处此处无法确定，故不标出处。褒义。

pinyin: qín jiǎn jiàn guó
literal: diligent · frugal · build · nation
natural: build the nation with diligence and thrift

meaning.en: A slogan urging hard work and thrift as the way to build up the country, popular in the early PRC and again in later campaigns.
meaning.zh: 口号，主张以勤劳节俭来建设国家，新中国成立初期和后来的运动中多次使用。

equivalents: build the nation through hard work and thrift
hard work and thrift build the country

examples.zh: 校门口贴着“勤俭建国”的老标语。
examples.en: An old 'build the nation with diligence and thrift' slogan is pasted at the school gate.

examples.zh: 他从小受“勤俭建国”的教育，一直省吃俭用。
examples.en: Raised on 'build the nation with diligence and thrift', he has lived frugally all his life.

usage.en: Often paired with 勤俭持家 ('manage the home with thrift'). Associated with Mao Zedong's calls in the 1950s for 勤俭建国 and 勤俭办一切事业, but the wording was also used by many others, so no origin is given. Positive, formal.
usage.zh: 常与“勤俭持家”对举。与毛泽东20世纪50年代提出的“勤俭建国”“勤俭办一切事业”相关，但许多人也用过这一说法，故不标出处。褒义，正式。

pinyin: yī qiè quán lì guī nóng huì
literal: all · power · belongs to · peasant association
natural: all power to the peasant associations

meaning.en: A slogan of the 1920s peasant movement in Hunan: village power should pass from landlords and gentry to the peasants' own associations.
meaning.zh: 20世纪20年代湖南农民运动的口号，主张乡村权力从地主豪绅手中转到农民协会。

equivalents: all power to the peasant associations

examples.zh: 历史教材引用“一切权力归农会”来说明农民运动的高涨。
examples.en: The history textbook quotes 'all power to the peasant associations' to show the surge of the peasant movement.

examples.zh: 课堂上，老师讲解了“一切权力归农会”的背景。
examples.en: In class the teacher explained the background of 'all power to the peasant associations'.

origin.source: 毛泽东《湖南农民运动考察报告》（1927年）

story.en: In his 1927 report on the Hunan peasant movement, Mao Zedong recorded that the peasants' associations took over rural authority, with the slogan 'all power to the peasant associations'.
story.zh: 毛泽东在1927年《湖南农民运动考察报告》中记述农民协会取得乡村权力，口号即“一切权力归农会”。

usage.en: A historical term for the 1926-27 rural movement. It is modelled on the Russian slogan 'all power to the Soviets'. Neutral, formal.
usage.zh: 对1926—1927年农村运动的历史用语。句式仿俄国“一切权力归苏维埃”。中性，正式。

pinyin: dà míng dà fàng
literal: greatly · speak out · greatly · bloom
natural: speak out and let it bloom, on a grand scale

meaning.en: A 1957 campaign term for speaking one's mind freely, in the Hundred Flowers movement, which was followed by the Anti-Rightist Campaign.
meaning.zh: 1957年“百花齐放、百家争鸣”运动中的用语，指畅所欲言，后来该运动被反右派斗争取代。

equivalents: to speak out freely
an open airing of views

examples.zh: 1957年的“大鸣大放”给许多知识分子带来了命运转折。
examples.en: The 'airing of views' of 1957 turned the fates of many intellectuals.

examples.zh: 会议开成了大鸣大放，大家都说出了心里话。
examples.en: The meeting turned into a free-for-all in which everyone said what they thought.

usage.en: Historical reference to 1957: 鸣 comes from 百家争鸣 and 放 from 百花齐放. Used today in history discussions, and occasionally in a light sense for a free exchange of views. Neutral, formal.
usage.zh: 对1957年的历史引用：“鸣”取自“百家争鸣”，“放”取自“百花齐放”。今天多见于历史讨论，偶尔也轻松地指畅所欲言。中性，正式。

pinyin: yī dà èr gōng
literal: first · large · second · public
natural: first, large; second, public

meaning.en: The principle of the 1958 people's communes: they should be as large in scale as possible and as publicly owned as possible.
meaning.zh: 1958年人民公社的原则：规模要大，公有化程度要高。

equivalents: bigger and more collective

examples.zh: 教科书说明了人民公社“一大二公”的特点。
examples.en: The textbook explains the 'large and public' character of the people's communes.

examples.zh: 研究者分析了“一大二公”对农村生产的影响。
examples.en: Researchers analysed the effects of the 'large and public' principle on farm output.

usage.en: A historical term from the Great Leap Forward (1958-60), used in history and economics. 大 means large scale and 公 means public ownership. Neutral, formal. No single originator is given.
usage.zh: 大跃进（1958—1960）时期的历史用语，见于历史和经济类文章。“大”指规模大，“公”指公有化程度高。中性，正式。不标明单一出处。
